name: hcapp_getInviteCode
description: Returns the invite code (HC.Hasher.ResetCode) for a target user so a kennel admin can share it with a member who has not yet set up the app. All of: the target has never signed in (LastLoginDateTime IS NULL and no HC.Device row — a web/portal sign-in creates one without the stamp, 2026-09-23; an invite code for a signed-in account is a takeover), the target is not removed, and the caller holds AppAccessFlags & 0x40000010 (manage members) on a kennel that is the target's HOME kennel. Otherwise errorCode 1312, errorType 13, with the reason ('not found', 'already signed in', 'not your home kennel') in the log and the user message (2026-10-04). Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 12, @param NULL). Read SP — no success envelope.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Passed to HC6.ValidateAppAuth for authentication.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived cryptographic token validated against DeviceSecret by HC6.ValidateAppAuth.

parameters.name: targetUserId
parameters.description: The Hasher.id of the user whose invite code is being requested.

rowsets.name: AuthError
rowsets.description: Returned when HC6.ValidateAppAuth fails (auth, device not found, etc.). Mutually exclusive with InviteCodeResult and PermissionError.

columns.name: errorId
columns.description: Unique ID of the HC.ErrorLog entry created by ValidateAppAuth.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: Specific error code set by ValidateAppAuth.

rowsets.name: PermissionError
rowsets.description: Returned when the code cannot be given — target not found or removed, already signed in (LastLoginDateTime set or an HC.Device row exists), or the caller lacks manage-members on the target's home kennel. errorCode 1312, errorType 13 in every case; the reason is in errorUserMessage and in the HC.ErrorLog row. Mutually exclusive with AuthError and InviteCodeResult.

columns.name: errorId
columns.description: Unique ID of the HC.ErrorLog entry created by this SP.

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: Always 13 in this SP (not found / permission denied).

columns.name: errorUserMessage
columns.description: One of three texts by reason: already signed in ('...can no longer be shown. They can sign in again with "Email me a new invite code".'), 'That member could not be found.', or 'Only an admin of this member's home kennel can see their invite code.'

rowsets.name: InviteCodeResult
rowsets.description: Returned on success — a single row with the target user's invite code. Mutually exclusive with AuthError and PermissionError.

columns.name: inviteCode
columns.description: The URC: prefixed reset code from HC.Hasher.ResetCode. Note: declared as NVARCHAR(250) in the SP but the table column is NVARCHAR(50). See code smells.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.ErrorLog on the 1312 path (lines 108-112, naming the target, the reason and their home kennel) and from the CATCH block (lines 133-135, after ROLLBACK)

codeSmells.detail: All three parameters (lines 3-5) have no SQL default. A client that omits @targetUserId gets 'expects parameter' — an unlogged empty 500 before the SP runs — rather than the logged 1312 'not found'.

codeSmells.issue: inviteCode variable wider than table column
codeSmells.detail: The SP declares @inviteCode as NVARCHAR(250), but HC.Hasher.ResetCode is NVARCHAR(50). The variable should match the table column to avoid silent implicit widening and misrepresentation in contracts.

The manage-members permission bitmask is embedded as a raw integer literal (1073741840) in the WHERE clause. There is no named constant, comment, or SP parameter to indicate what right is being checked. Should be documented clearly or extracted to a named constant.

Lines 99-106 work out which condition failed but all three return errorCode 1312 / errorType 13 (line 107); only errorUserMessage differs. A client that wants to branch (e.g. offer 'email a new code' only for the signed-in case) must match the text.

breakingChanges: Auth failure now returns the standard HC6 error rowset (errorId, errorType, errorCode, errorTitle, errorUserMessage, errorProc) instead of HC5's non-standard Pascal-cased rowset (ErrorType, ErrorTitle, ErrorDescription).
Permission/not-found failure now returns the standard HC6 error rowset with errorCode=1312 instead of HC5's 'No valid user' string in the result column.
Success rowset column is now named 'inviteCode' instead of HC5's 'result'.

HC5 returned a single rowset in all cases (success or failure) with the same column name 'result'; HC6 returns structurally different rowsets for success vs error — callers must check for the presence of errorId or inviteCode to distinguish.
